page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARMv8 architecture. It features 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. There is no bundled local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration included with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate that the single-core performance of the Neoverse-N1 processor is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48, placing it in the average tier. However, due to having only a single vCPU and thread, multi-core benchmarks like stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 11.99 GB/sec and write speeds at 7.95 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware AES acceleration, though extended instruction tests show lower throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a highly accessible entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, providing dedicated CPU resources without the performance variability of shared-core configurations. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, small-scale development environments, or low-traffic utility services that do not require high memory bandwidth or parallel processing capabilities.
